about.en:
Leadership in the Business World (LBW) is a selective residential summer programme run by the Wharton School's Global Youth Program. Students attend lectures by Wharton faculty, visit companies, hear from business leaders and work in teams on a business plan that they pitch to a panel of judges at the end of the session.

The 2027 programme runs in three three-week sessions (6–26 June, 27 June–17 July, 18 July–7 August 2027) in Philadelphia, with around 120 students selected per session. It is designed for students currently in grade 11 with demonstrated leadership experience and an unweighted GPA of at least 3.5; international applicants are explicitly welcome.

The 2027 fee is USD 12,299 (plus a USD 100 application fee). Admissions are need-blind, but fee waivers and most scholarships are restricted to specific groups (Philadelphia students, partner nominees, Caribbean access), so most international students should expect to pay in full.

about.en:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three prepare an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music and literature, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (team quiz). Rounds also include social events such as a talent show and Scholar's Ball.

The Rabat round takes place on 22–23 January 2027 at Rabat American School. Students can take part through a school club or independently with at least two teammates; regional rounds are open to students from any country, and good results qualify teams for the next Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.

Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for the Global Round and Yale Tournament of Champions

Attend the round in Rabat on 22–23 January 2027

Teams of three prepare an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music and literature, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (team quiz). Rounds also include social events such as a talent show and Scholar's Ball.

The Cairo round takes place on 16–17 April 2027 at Cairo American College. Students can take part through a school club or independently with at least two teammates; regional rounds are open to students from any country, and good results qualify teams for the next Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.

en: Four team events: debate, writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for the Global Round and Yale Tournament of Champions

eligibility.en: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; students may enter independently without a school club.

Attend the round in Cairo on 16–17 April 2027

costs.en: Registration fee per student set by WSC for each round (not shown on the calendar page); travel and accommodation extra.

about.en:
Emory Pre-College offers two-week, non-credit courses taught by Emory faculty and graduate students in subjects ranging from neuroscience, medicine and psychology to creative writing, business and law. Residential students live in Emory dorms in Atlanta and join social and cultural activities; Emory also runs a separate Pre-Med Institute and a credit-bearing Summer College.

In 2027 the Pre-College sessions run 13–26 June, 27 June–10 July and 11–24 July. The programme is for current high-school sophomores and juniors. Applications open in December 2026 and close on 3 May 2027 (popular courses fill earlier). Anyone who is not a US citizen or permanent resident applies as an international applicant, with English proficiency shown by SAT/ACT scores, TOEFL 104 / IELTS 7.5 or a competitive Duolingo score, plus a writing sample.

about.en:
Barnard Pre-College runs summer institutes on its campus next to Columbia University in Manhattan. The NextGen Leadership Institute combines a three-week academic strand (Scientific Exploration, Literature & Performing Arts or Global Humanities) with leadership workshops; the Health & Society Institute looks at how culture, policy and inequality shape health; and the Athena Summer Innovation Institute guides teams through venture development to a final pitch.

Sessions run 28 June–16 July and 19 July–6 August 2027 (Athena in Session I only). Applications open 1 December 2026, the financial-aid and fee-waiver deadline is 15 February 2027 and the final deadline 15 April 2027. International students may enrol in these non-credit institutes (not the credit-bearing Pre-Baccalaureate), live in residence halls, pay the same tuition as US students and do not need an English test, but Barnard does not offer them financial aid or I-20 visa sponsorship.

The Stanford Summer Humanities Institute is a residential programme in which small groups of high-school students spend three weeks in an intensive seminar on a humanities topic (philosophy, history, literature, politics and similar) led by a Stanford professor, supported by graduate-student instructors. Students read primary texts, debate in seminar, write a research paper and live on the Stanford campus.

The programme is for rising high-school juniors and seniors (grades 10–11 at the time of application). In 2026 it ran in two sessions (21 June–10 July and 12–31 July) with an application deadline of 2 February 2026; the 2027 dates should follow a similar pattern. about.en:
Future of the Business World is an intensive online programme from Wharton Global Youth for students around the world. Each weekday includes two hours of live lectures and one hour of TA-led recitation, plus simulations, small-group work and independent study; students choose a morning (08:00–11:00 EDT) or afternoon (13:00–16:00 EDT) block. Topics include design thinking, scenario planning, market research and business communication, and teams finish with a project predicting future business trends.

2027 sessions run 14–25 June and 5–16 July. The programme is for students currently in grades 9–12; the priority deadline is 27 January 2027, after which admission is rolling. Completers receive a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion.

about.en:
African Leadership Academy (ALA) is a two-year residential school near Johannesburg that brings together young people from across Africa and around the world to prepare for university and for leadership on the continent. Students live on campus with peers from many countries and follow a programme built around academic readiness and leadership development.

For the 2027 entry, applicants must be born on or after 1 September 2007; nationality is not a restriction. Applications opened on 15 July 2026; the Early Decision deadline (15 October) has passed, and the Regular Decision deadline is 15 January 2027, with results in April 2027. Selection is holistic (intellectual readiness, courage and perseverance, ownership, interdependence). The all-inclusive cost is USD 30,900 a year, but every admitted student is eligible for need-based aid and 97% receive financial assistance.
